intro: Press reports, minutes and academic texts report what others said in indirect speech with Konjunktiv I. It signals 'this is their claim, not mine' without any verb of saying in every sentence. The forms come from the infinitive stem: er habe, sie sei, man könne, es werde, er müsse, sie halte. Konjunktiv I is only clearly visible in the third person singular (and with sein in every person); where it looks exactly like the indicative (sie haben, wir müssen, sie werden), German switches to Konjunktiv II: sie hätten, sie müssten, sie würden. The past is formed with the Konjunktiv of haben or sein plus the participle (er habe gesehen, sie sei abgereist, der Antrag sei genehmigt worden), the future with werde + infinitive. Questions keep ob or their w-word with the verb at the end (ob die Finanzierung gesichert sei), and commands become sollen (advice, instruction) or mögen (polite request): er solle sich schonen, man möge sich kurz fassen.
tips[0].title: Konjunktiv I = stem + e
tips[0].text: Third person singular: stem + e, no umlaut, no vowel change. sein is irregular in every person.
tips[0].check.why: Konjunktiv I is the stem + e with no umlaut: fahr + e = er fahre. It differs from the indicative, so it stays.
tips[1].title: Replacement by Konjunktiv II
tips[1].text: When Konjunktiv I is identical to the indicative (mostly the plural and ich-forms), use Konjunktiv II; if that is identical to the Präteritum as well, use würde + infinitive.
tips[1].trap: Do not replace a distinct Konjunktiv I in formal writing: er habe, not er hätte; es sei, not es wäre. Spoken German often uses Konjunktiv II everywhere, but a press report or formal text expects Konjunktiv I where it exists.
tips[1].check.why: Konjunktiv I sie haben looks exactly like the indicative, so Konjunktiv II steps in: sie hätten.
tips[2].title: Past and future
tips[2].text: There is only one past in indirect speech: habe/sei + Partizip II, whatever tense the original used. The future uses werde + infinitive (plural: würden).
tips[2].check.why: Indirect speech has one past: habe/sei + Partizip II, whatever tense the original used. verlassen takes haben, and er habe is a distinct Konjunktiv I.
tips[2].visual.rows[0].b: Er sagte, er habe es gewusst.
tips[3].title: Questions and commands
tips[3].text: Yes/no questions → ob; w-questions keep the w-word; the verb goes to the end. Imperatives → sollen (instruction, advice) or mögen (polite request).
tips[3].check.why: A yes/no question is reported with ob, and the verb goes to the end of the clause.
tips[3].visual.rows[1].b: Er wollte wissen, wann die Sitzung beginne.
tips[3].visual.rows[2].b: Sie sagte, ich solle hier warten.

remember[0]: Third person singular: habe, sei, werde, könne, müsse — never hätte/wäre where these exist.
remember[1]: Plural: haben/werden/müssen look like the indicative → hätten/würden/müssten.
mistakes[0].why: sie haben is identical to the indicative, so Konjunktiv II is needed.
mistakes[1].why: The third person singular has a distinct Konjunktiv I; formal texts use it.
mistakes[2].why: Indirect speech has one past tense: habe/sei + Partizip II.
mistakes[3].why: Indirect yes/no questions need ob and verb-final order.
hook: Er sagte, er habe …: one small vowel lets a news report pass on a claim without vouching for it.
